transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-10-09
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Recorded on: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Tom Avery (CTO - Helixogen), Rashida Khan (Director IT), Emily Cho (Head of ML), Diego Marquez (Security Architect)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
- Scoping POC to validate PrivateLink vs VPC peering for Helixogen's inference workloads; primary constraints are data residency (EU/US split), no egress allowed for inference payloads, and SOC2/KMS requirements.
- Success criteria: p95 latency target, concurrency/throughput targets, audit log access, and zero-data-exfiltration proof.
- Next: Redwood to run benchmarks on private path, Helixogen to share prompt set and VPC details.

Topics: network topology, PrivateLink vs VPC peering, egress control, benchmarks (latency, throughput), test dataset, timeline and procurement items

[00:00:05] Jordan (AE): All right folks, thanks for taking the time. Quick intro — Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AM on this. Priya is our SE, she'll lead the benchmark plan. Could each of you intro briefly?

[00:00:20] Tom (Helixogen): Tom here, CTO, we run internal LLM-powered clinical summarization pipelines. Sensitive PHI-like metadata, so residency and egress are a hard stop.

[00:00:30] Rashida: Rashida — I run infra. We're heavily VPC peering'd across us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Procurement wants minimal public egress, ideally PrivateLink or VPC peering with strict egress rules.

[00:00:40] Emily: Emily — ML lead. We need stable latency for a chat UX and batch embeddings for indexing. Typical inference sizes: 1-3k tokens often, occasional 8k token jobs for reports.

[00:00:55] Diego: Diego — security. SOC2 in place, but I need to confirm KMS/HSM integration, audit logging, and proof that data does not cross region or leak to third-party telemetry.

[00:01:10] Priya (SE): Great, thanks. Today we'll align on success criteria, network path options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), bench workloads, and timeline. We'll also flag any procurement/security blockers.

[00:01:35] Jordan: Quick note — Helixogen's constraint "no egress" means we need to validate that payloads and tokenized data never transit outside the customer's VPC/region. We'll talk about our Private (VPC) deployment options that support that.

[00:02:00] Tom: Curious, when you say Private deployments, do you mean Redwood Private in our VPC or Dedicated capacity hosted in Redwood but peered? What's the difference practically?

[00:02:12] Priya: Good question. Short answer: Private (VPC) is our control-plane-in-Redwood but compute running in your VPC or customer-managed VPC endpoints; Dedicated is reserved GPUs in Redwood's infra — usually requires peering and egress rules. For strict no-egress, PrivateLink into a deployment inside your VPC or our on-prem option is recommended.

[00:02:40] Rashida: So PrivateLink would give us an interface endpoint and traffic stays within AWS backbone? That would satisfy legal?

[00:02:48] Priya: Yes, with AWS PrivateLink the interface endpoint ensures traffic does not go over the public internet. We still need to confirm region placement (you said eu and us regions). PrivateLink endpoints are regional, so you'd provision endpoints in each region.

[00:03:05] Diego: Any telemetry/ops data sent back to Redwood control plane? Is that encrypted and can it be disabled? We need to know what metadata is shared.

[00:03:18] Jordan: We have a control plane that receives health telemetry. For Private deployments we can minimize telemetry and we support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest. Priya, can you expand?

[00:03:28] Priya: Briefly: we can send only aggregated non-PII metrics; detailed logs and request traces can be kept in-customer VPC and forwarded to their S3/CloudWatch. We also have an option to disable some telemetry for compliance. We'll share the exact telemetry table.

[00:03:50] Emily: From benchmarks perspective — what sample sizes and metrics do you typically run for a POC? We need to ensure we stress the long-tail 8k token jobs.

[00:03:59] Priya: We'll do three scenarios: 1) low-latency chat 1-3k tokens at steady QPS to get p50/p95/p99 latency; 2) batch embeddings throughput run (100-500 reqs per second with batching); 3) long-context generation 8k tokens to measure memory/KV cache behavior. We'll also track cost per 1k tokens and KV cache hit rates.

[00:04:25] Tom: Our peak concurrency is around 120 concurrent sessions for a particular service, but typical steady-state is 30-40. We also have nightly batch indexing jobs that need to hit 400 embeddings/sec.

[00:04:37] Priya: Noted. For the chat workload we'll emulate a burst profile: baseline 40 QPS with spikes to 120 QPS sustained for up to 20 minutes. For embeddings we'll run ramp tests to 500 RPS and watch GPU utilization.

[00:04:55] Rashida: Network-wise: we prefer PrivateLink because it avoids cross-account route table changes and keeps traffic private. But peering is okay if it's limited and we control egress. Also curious about VPC endpoints in eu-west-1 — any capacity constraints?

[00:05:10] Priya: Capacity depends on whether we use Redwood Dedicated in region or provision Private nodes in your account. We do have capacity in eu-west-1 but for guaranteed throughput we recommend a Dedicated reservation or deploying a small cluster in your VPC for the POC. We'll include capacity options in the plan.

[00:05:30] Diego: On KMS: we need customer-managed keys and HSM-backed key stores. Can Redwood use our CMKs?

[00:05:38] Priya: Yes, we support CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) for data at rest when using Private deployments. We'll link the KMS integration guide.

[00:05:50] Tom: Audit logs: we need per-request logging for a sample window, with redaction. Is that supported?

[00:05:57] Jordan: We can produce detailed audit logs stored in your CloudWatch/S3, and we can implement field-level redaction. We'll need to agree on retention and what fields are captured.

[00:06:10] Emily: Success criteria from our side — can we enumerate? I propose: (1) p95 latency < 300ms for chat at baseline 40 QPS; (2) embeddings throughput >= 400 RPS with cost estimate; (3) long-context generation p95 < 2.5s for 8k tokens (this is soft); (4) proof that no payload leaves eu-west-1 for EU customers; (5) verified KMS/CMEK + audit logs available.

[00:06:38] Jordan: That sounds good. I'll capture those as the POC success criteria and send back a written version. Anything to add?

[00:06:45] Diego: Add penetration test checklist — we may want a narrow window to run a security scan against the deployment. Also need an SLA for availability during the POC window.

[00:06:55] Priya: We can provide an agreed uptime target during the benchmark window and coordinate maintenance windows. Pen tests are OK if scheduled; we ask for a test plan ahead of time.

[00:07:10] Tom: Timeline — what's realistic? We need to have a short POC to prove residency and latency within 3-4 weeks due to procurement timing.

[00:07:18] Jordan: For targeted POC I think 3-6 weeks is realistic: week 1 network setup + IAM/KMS, week 2 deploy and smoke tests, week 3 run benchmarks and validate success criteria, week 4 buffer for repeat runs and security scans. If procurement moves fast we can compress.

[00:07:36] Rashida: For week 1 we'll need a CloudFormation or Terraform snippet for PrivateLink endpoints and IAM roles. Diego will also need the minimal set of IPs/ports.

[00:07:45] Priya: We'll provide a PrivateLink CF template and a peering checklist. We'll also include security groups, required NACLs, and recommended route table entries.

[00:07:55] Diego: Egress constraints: we require that egress only goes to our internal S3 endpoints and that no third-party telemetry endpoints are reachable. Can Redwood lock down egress?

[00:08:04] Priya: On Private deployments inside your VPC, you control egress policies. For Dedicated hosted by Redwood with peering, we enforce egress through controlled NATs and can apply allow-lists. We'll document both options and recommended egress ACLs.

[00:08:22] Emily: Benchmarks — what tooling do you use? JMeter? Locust? Something GPU-aware?

[00:08:29] Priya: We typically use a mix: custom load runner that simulates realistic token distributions, Locust for concurrency patterns, and a GPU profiler to capture utilization, memory, and latency tails. We'll share the runner repo.

[00:08:42] Tom: Can we run a dry run with synthetic data before giving you the real prompt set? Procurement requires data minimization.

[00:08:49] Jordan: Absolutely. Start with synthetic anonymized prompts, then run the same tests with the anonymized real prompts. We'll support both.

[00:08:58] Rashida: One more on regions: we have EU customers so data for EU must be pinned to eu-west-1. Are you able to deploy dedicated nodes in that region for the POC with PrivateLink endpoints?

[00:09:09] Priya: Yes, we can provision nodes in eu-west-1. For guaranteed performance we either reserve dedicated capacity or run compute in your VPC via our Private package. We'll include both cost and lead-time in the follow-up.

[00:09:25] Diego: CD process: we'll need to sign an MSA addendum for the POC covering data handling and liability. Who from Redwood legal will engage?

[00:09:33] Jordan: I'll loop in our legal lead. In the meantime I'll send the standard POC addendum template.

[00:09:42] Emily: For metrics — can you collect KV cache hit rates? That's important for long-context cost savings.

[00:09:48] Priya: Yep, we'll instrument KV cache hits/misses, batch sizes, and token counts. Our console will show token breakdown per request and aggregate cost estimates.

[00:09:58] Tom: Cost — can we get an estimate for the POC run? Ballpark is fine but we need to budget.

[00:10:05] Jordan: We'll send a POC cost estimate after we size the cluster for your concurrency and token distribution. Expect a separate pricing note: PrivateLink + Dedicated nodes vs Private-in-VPC pricing.

[00:10:15] Rashida: Procurement also wants to know if any open-source models are used and what quantization/FP16 tradeoffs exist. We may require determinism for audits.

[00:10:24] Priya: We'll list model variants. For the POC we'll use a Redwood-verified open model with a quantized variant for cost testing and an FP16 variant for performance testing. We'll capture any nondeterminism notes.

[00:10:36] Diego: Are there any service endpoints that require public egress (e.g., licensing checks)?

[00:10:42] Priya: No licensing calls in the hot path — it's all offline. Control plane registration happens once; we can do a staged offline registration if needed.

[00:10:50] Jordan: Let's summarize the agreed POC plan and acceptance criteria. I'll type it here and share after the call.

[00:11:00] Jordan (summary):
- Objective: validate private networking and data residency for Helixogen inference workloads and meet performance targets.
- Success criteria: p95 chat <300ms at 40 QPS baseline; embeddings >=400 RPS; long-context p95 <2.5s (soft); no egress for EU traffic; KMS/CMEK + audit logs verified; penetration test allowed in scheduled window.
- Benchmarks: three scenarios (chat, embeddings, long-context) with both synthetic and anonymized prompt sets.
- Network: prefer PrivateLink endpoints in each region; alternate option VPC peering with strict egress controls.
- Timeline: target 3-6 weeks (network setup week1, deploy+smoke week2, benchmark week3, buffer week4).

[00:11:38] Tom: Sounds good. A couple quick clarifications: for the long-context runs do you support dynamic KV cache warmup? We want to model repeated conversation continuation.

[00:11:47] Priya: Yes we can script warmup sequences to pre-populate KV caches and measure steady-state vs cold-start latencies. We'll include that in the benchmark plan.

[00:11:58] Rashida: Diego will send the CIDRs and the security contact.

[00:12:04] Diego: I'll send those by EOD Monday, and I'll attach our minimal pentest rules and SCIM/SSO requirements.

[00:12:12] Priya: Great; I'll draft the benchmark scenarios and share a doc. Jordan will send pricing and MSA addendum.

[00:12:20] Jordan: Next steps recap: 1) Redwood sends PrivateLink CF template + KMS guide + telemetry table; 2) Helixogen shares CIDRs and anonymized prompt set; 3) SE builds benchmark plan and we schedule run for week of 2025-10-20.

[00:12:35] Tom: One ask — can Redwood provide sample logs showing audit trail format so our compliance team can pre-approve?

[00:12:43] Priya: Yes we'll attach sample audit logs (redacted) and the schema in the follow-up email.

[00:12:50] Jordan: Anything else before we wrap?

[00:12:55] Rashida: No, that's it. Thanks everyone.

[00:13:00] Tom: Thanks — appreciate it.

[00:13:05] Meeting closed
